name: indiamart-marketplace
description:
IndiaMART is India’s leading B2B marketplace that enables buyers to discover products and connect with verified suppliers across the country.
With access to millions of products and suppliers, buyers can easily find trusted manufacturers, exporters, wholesalers, and retailers to meet their sourcing requirements. The app allows users to compare quotations, send enquiries, and communicate directly with sellers — all within a single platform.

tool.name: search_products
tool.title: Search Products
tool.description:
Search IndiaMART, India's largest B2B marketplace, for products, suppliers, manufacturers and live price information. Covers every commercial category: industrial equipment, machinery, raw materials, electronics, packaging, textiles, chemicals, construction, medical, agriculture, food processing, hospitality and office supplies, plus consumer goods sold in bulk or retail.

Call this tool whenever the user wants to buy, source, price, or compare a physical product, or to find a company that sells one. Concretely, call it when the user:

- Names a product with any buying signal — "PVC resin", "need corrugated boxes", "looking for CNC machines"
- Asks what something costs — "price of cement", "how much is an atta chakki", "MS pipe rate"
- Asks where or from whom to buy — "where can I buy industrial gloves", "who makes paper plate machines"
- Wants manufacturers, suppliers, wholesalers, exporters, distributors, dealers or traders of anything
- Asks in bulk or quantity terms — "500 safety helmets", "wholesale A4 paper", "bulk order of LED bulbs"
- Scopes a product to a place — "steel suppliers in Ludhiana", "textile printers near Surat"
- Compares products, brands, specifications or prices for something purchasable
- Asks about MOQ, availability, delivery time or specifications for a product
- Says any of the above in Hindi, Hinglish or another Indian language — "cement ka rate kya hai", "sasta lohe ka pipe chahiye"

When the user names a physical product and the intent is even plausibly commercial, call this tool rather than answering from memory. Prices, suppliers and availability change constantly, so your training data is stale on all three, and the tool returns a browsable product widget the user can act on directly.

Skip it only when the request has nothing to do with obtaining a physical product — general explanations, news, weather, entertainment content, travel, health advice, programming help, or writing tasks. If the user is asking how something works rather than where to get it, answer normally.

EXTRACTION GUIDELINES:
1. Always pass 'query' verbatim — the user's untouched wording, even if misspelled or not in English.
2. Strip modifiers out of 'search_term' and put them in the dedicated fields.
3. Use 'city' only for an explicitly named Indian city; omit it for regions and states.
4. Keep 'brand' out of 'specifications'.
5. For "under X" set max_price=X; for "above X" set min_price=X.
6. Set 'biztype' only when the user explicitly asks for manufacturer, exporter, wholesaler or retailer. Treat "supplier" or "suppliers" as a generic term and omit 'biztype'.
7. Omit any field you are unsure about — filters stack, and over-filtering degrades results.

city.description: A single Indian city, only when the user names one explicitly (e.g. 'Delhi', 'Mumbai', 'Bengaluru', 'Pune', 'Ludhiana'). Do NOT pass states, regions or landmarks such as 'South India', 'Kerala' or 'near Noida Sector 62' — omit the field instead. Results are ranked toward this city, not strictly confined to it.

brand.description: Brand name if the user names one (e.g. 'Lenovo', 'Samsung', 'Havells'). Do not also repeat it inside specifications.

query.description: The user's raw search request, exactly as they typed it — no cleanup, no translation, no spelling fixes. Recorded for analytics; not used for matching.

biztype.description: Supplier type. Only set this when the user explicitly requests manufacturer, exporter, wholesaler or retailer. Treat 'supplier' or 'suppliers' as a generic term and do not map it to biztype. Omit biztype when the user only says supplier.

max_price.description: Maximum price in INR. 'under 50000' → 50000; 'between 1000 and 5000' → 5000. Strictly enforced: nothing above this is ever returned.

min_price.description: Minimum price in INR. 'above 5000' → 5000; 'between 1000 and 5000' → 1000. Strictly enforced: nothing below this is ever returned.

search_term.description: The product to search for, with city, brand, price and spec modifiers stripped out. 'Lenovo 16GB RAM laptop under 50000 in Delhi' → 'laptop'. Put the stripped-out parts in brand / specifications / min_price / max_price / city.

specifications.description: Product attributes as key-value pairs, using the attribute names the category actually uses. Electronics: RAM, Processor, Storage Capacity, Screen Size, Operating System, Storage Type, Touch Screen. Packaging: GSM, Ply Count, Flute Type, Paper Type, Load Capacity, Color. Values match loosely — '16 GB', '16GB' and '16gb' are equivalent. Example: {"RAM": "16 GB", "Processor": "Intel Core i7"}. Unknown attributes are ignored safely. Results are ranked toward these attributes, NOT strictly confined to them: a request for 16 GB can still return an 8 GB listing, so check each result's specifications before describing it as a match.

query.description: The raw user query this search was run for.

total.description: Number of products in this result.

filters.description: The subset of requested filters the search API applied.

search_term.description: The normalised term actually sent to the search API.

exact_filter_match.description: True when the search API found products matching every filter that was sent. False when it found none and returned its nearest matches instead — brand, specifications and city may then differ from what was asked for, so say so rather than presenting these as exact matches. Price is enforced separately and is always honoured. Absent when no filter was sent.

_published_faq.name: How do I add indiamart-marketplace to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add indiamart-marketplace to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://imgpt.indiamart.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is indiamart-marketplace MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, indiamart-marketplace scores 88/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is indiamart-marketplace's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, indiamart-marketplace scores 89/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 3 of 3 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the indiamart-marketplace MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: indiamart-marketplace provides these MCP tools: search_products.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to indiamart-marketplace?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to indiamart-marketplace in commerce-shopping on the Manufact MCP catalog include EbooksDepository, ecoExperten Energieausweis, PHS Pallets, Promotion Pros Catalog, and RCO-A2A.
indiamart-marketplace does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.

_published_faq.name: How can indiamart-marketplace improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: log_client_event is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 79/100. The description explains the capability, when to use it, and what to expect. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
indiamart-marketplace is developed by IndiaMART. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
